ageInterpretation: Official Grades 1–2 early-primary window; printed source grades retained separately, no invented per-grade deadlines.
designStatus: Original source-fit task and material specifications; not learner observations or a claim every component task establishes whole-topic mastery.

protocols.task: Use English letters in mixed order and familiar word contexts, distinguishing the letter name from a common speech sound. Link selected basic sounds to their written forms.
evidenceDesign: Retain actual alphabet knowledge and sound-symbol association as different responses.
For the complete existing claims, include both cases, alphabet order, letter-name spelling choices, consonant sounds and short/long vowel examples.
Accept appropriate local English pronunciation; do not impose an unrelated script inventory.
nearMisses: Only singing the alphabet in fixed order without recognising a shown letter.
Giving a letter name when a different speech sound is requested.
protocols.transfer: Change order, case and familiar word context.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete letter/single-letter-sound claims are appropriate to this named-English source; they are not universal R1/R2 letter claims. No one-source success automatically certifies all letters/sounds or transfers to another language.

protocols.task: Say familiar English word parts in two or three spoken syllables, without an answer picture; the child joins them to say the word. Add counting, oral separation and written-word pronunciation support for the complete Syllables claim.
evidenceDesign: Include both two- and three-part sequences and a new familiar word.
Distinguish joining spoken units from naming letters or decoding a printed long word.
Keep both repeated printed source positions and their separate IDs.
nearMisses: Reciting one memorised sequence or counting visible letters.
protocols.transfer: Join a new familiar word with a different syllable pattern.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The existing oral-analysis claim includes more than this source component. Its additional cases are supplied separately; no second topic is created for the repeated position.

protocols.task: Invite the child to choose something to write about and attempt its written label/message using the sounds they hear. Ask what it says and how a chosen letter represents a heard sound; preserve the original attempt before optional shared revision.
evidenceDesign: Retain actual child-authored production, not only willingness or a positive feeling.
Notice phonically plausible representations without requiring untaught conventional spellings; assess accurate simple taught-word encoding separately for the complete spelling-by-sound claim.
Offer low-stakes choice and support; record access, prompts and contextual response rather than score enjoyment.
nearMisses: Adult writes the entire word while the activity is credited to the child.
Arbitrary copied letters without the child connecting them to intended sounds.
Treating nonstandard but plausible encoding as a stable inability or correct conventional spelling.
protocols.transfer: Invite an independently chosen second word/message and ask about a different sound choice.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: BhY contributes actual phonemic encoding. An inventive attempt alone does not establish its complete conventional CVC/simple-word spelling or the whole inherited phonics terminology inventory. The contextual channel is neither removed nor inferred from correct performance.

protocols.task: Use a genuinely matched English book and a declared collection of familiar high-frequency/exception words. Check first reading, rereading and a second changed text.
evidenceDesign: Distinguish automatic recognition from decoding and from guessing by picture.
Check meaningful connected reading and improved pace/expression after rereading.
For the complete sight-word claim, include its 20–30 familiar high-frequency-word evidence and unusual spelling/sound discussion; this is not an invented NCERT universal word list.
nearMisses: Only recognising a memorised book cover or repeating an adult-read page.
protocols.transfer: Read a new matched passage with different word order.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete basic-reading and sight-word operations are retained. Registered intrinsic corrections permit matched emergent reading without requiring the whole 40+ inventory first; English print direction remains appropriate here.

protocols.task: Say familiar English word sets and a short poem/refrain. Ask the child to identify a genuine audible rhyme, supply another and join or recall a repeated line.
evidenceDesign: Judge the actual spoken ending in the child’s English variety rather than final spelling alone.
Include a non-rhyming near match and a genuine rhyme with different initial sounds.
Retain whole-claim rhyme production, refrain participation and a short learned poem case.
nearMisses: Selecting words only because their printed endings look alike.
Accepting the adult-supplied answer without a changed example.
protocols.transfer: Use a new word family and a new short refrain.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Rhyme recognition, production and participation are existing shared operations; no separate country, word-family or receptive-only clone is needed.

protocols.task: Read and compose brief meaningful English sentences. Contrast an ordinary statement, question and exclamation; for the Grade 2 comma position, include a sentence listing at least three familiar items.
evidenceDesign: For Grade 1, explicitly check the stated sentence-ending marks; broader whole-claim checks retain capitals and exclamation use.
For Grade 2, interpret/use all named mark types, including a basic list-comma function; do not import advanced clause punctuation.
Explain how a mark helps the reader and repair a deliberately mispunctuated example.
nearMisses: Naming a shape without understanding its use.
Putting a comma after every word or a question mark after every sentence.
protocols.transfer: Choose punctuation for a new sentence and repair a different list.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete starting/ending-sentence and list-comma claims are retained, with sentence-building prerequisite tasks as needed. Source comprehension alone is not a certificate of complete independent punctuation writing.

protocols.task: Hear an English poem within the actual printed source range: Grade 1’s selected position uses 4–8 lines, and Grade 2’s combined listening/rhyme position uses 8–12. Ask for literal meaning/key details before sound-pattern discussion.
evidenceDesign: Use questions, paraphrase, action or picture selection that reveal actual spoken-text meaning without scripting every response.
Retain the Grade 2 combined rhyme requirement through its linked rhyme task.
For the separate literal-meaning position, do not substitute expressive voice or rhyme detection for understanding.
nearMisses: A memorised recitation with no understanding.
Giving the answer by picture before checking the heard words.
protocols.transfer: Hear another appropriately bounded poem with different details.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole listening claim spans poetry, narrative and non-fiction beyond independent reading, so suitable short heard-story/factual cases remain available separately. This source task does not require independent decoding.

protocols.task: Use a short English chant, song and poem with a repeated beat or sound pattern. Invite rhythmic participation, noticing a rhyme and a response about an interesting pattern.
evidenceDesign: Clap/tap the beat and join a repeated pattern at the appropriate point.
Distinguish audible rhyme from merely repeating any final word.
Invite an aesthetic response without requiring a prescribed positive feeling.
nearMisses: Accurate clapping treated as the only evidence of word/rhyme understanding.
Demanding visible enthusiasm.
protocols.transfer: Change rhythm and word endings in another short text.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete rhythm and rhyme claims retain replication, recognition/production and refrain/recitation cases; unfamiliar source wording does not justify a new rhythm topic.

protocols.task: Use a familiar free-choice exchange for the Grade 1 position and a supplied meaningful scenario for Grade 2. The child listens, takes and gives turns and responds to the actual partner.
evidenceDesign: Maintain several relevant turns and repair misunderstanding.
A scenario may supply the situation, not every spoken response.
Judge intelligibility and connectedness without a native accent/speed target.
nearMisses: Repeating both sides of a rehearsed dialogue.
Only contributing once while never yielding or responding.
protocols.transfer: Change partner and familiar purpose.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete discussion claim includes sustained attention, topic continuity and building on others; the description component adds clearly organised details where linked.

protocols.task: Invite the child to describe a familiar event or idea, wonder about an alternative and try a useful new English word while explaining their thinking.
evidenceDesign: Retain child-selected ideas and connected detail rather than only repeat a sentence model.
Include a speculative or imagined possibility and a meaningful vocabulary attempt for the full exploratory-talk claim.
Record prompting and help separately from independent expression.
nearMisses: Adult selects every idea and dictates the exact response.
protocols.transfer: Discuss another familiar event with a different possible explanation.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete descriptive and exploratory-talk operations remain intact; expressing ideas freely does not require positive mood or a particular personality style.

protocols.task: Use immediate simple English commands and a connected safe multi-step sequence. Include an actual relay to a peer for the relevant Grade 1 position, then an independently given sequence and ambiguity repair for the complete existing claim.
evidenceDesign: Retain the source distinction between acting on a command, relaying instructions and giving a connected sequence.
Check order and an actual result, not only repeat the action words.
For the whole claim, follow four steps, request clarification, give ordered instructions and repair unclear wording.
nearMisses: Success on one command credited as complete multi-step instruction mastery.
Repeating an adult sequence without a peer acting on its meaning.
protocols.transfer: Use a different drawing or material activity and a changed ambiguity.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete instruction operation is retained, with the registered question-word correction. Source relay success alone does not establish independent instruction authorship; all additional whole-claim checks are separate.

protocols.task: Hear an unfamiliar-to-task English narrative, then discuss people, ordered events and relevant details. For the Grade 2 interaction position, ask and answer meaningful questions in English.
evidenceDesign: Separate heard comprehension from independent decoding.
Require relevant responses to a changed story detail rather than only recite memorised names.
For the mixed Grade 1 position, retain a separate low-stakes engagement/access channel without inferring enjoyment from correct answers.
nearMisses: Naming only a cover picture or repeating the adult’s answer.
protocols.transfer: Hear a new narrative with different people and event relations.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete read-aloud and story-element claims include key tales, settings, sequence, clarification and non-fiction/poetry listening cases. These remain separate whole-claim tasks; no written-narrative prerequisite is added.

protocols.task: Provide an accessible actual opportunity for the relevant spelling play, chosen recitation or story encounter. Invite a low-stakes response about the activity and allow changing preference, hesitation or frustration.
evidenceDesign: Retain the actual skill/production/performance task in the linked protocol; do not reduce a mixed source requirement to attitude alone.
Separate access and support from response; do not create a stable learner feeling label or score.
Correct performance does not prove enjoyment and reluctance does not prove lack of skill.
nearMisses: Forced liking, a positive-feelings compliance rule or a quota of enthusiastic responses.
Only offering an activity without retaining its actual skill evidence design.
protocols.transfer: Offer a different accessible text or production choice after another interval.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The three mixed records keep component claims plus contextual evidence design. They are not relabelled pure mastery or excluded from the source; no learner state field or validated attitude scale is introduced.

protocols.task: Invite an oral retelling with clear people and an ordered event line, then a short account for a listener who did not hear the original.
evidenceDesign: Retain enough descriptive detail and organisation for a listener to follow.
Distinguish a retelling from independent original authorship and from merely repeating disconnected sentences.
Use a different ending or detail question to check control of meaning.
nearMisses: Adult supplies each next event while the response is labelled an independent telling.
protocols.transfer: Retell a different familiar short narrative to a new listener.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete story-element and clear-description claims include settings, key details, temporal order and intelligible expression. Written developed narrative is a different operation and is not imposed.

protocols.task: Use English words for familiar objects, experiences and classroom purposes in meaningful exchanges: express a need/choice, ask or tell, and respond or clarify. Add a short written application when assessing the complete existing vocabulary claim.
evidenceDesign: Check appropriate meaning in varied situations, not only repeat a definition.
Record whether a word was already known, introduced or prompted.
Do not infer English word knowledge from another role language, or invent a universal word-count threshold.
nearMisses: A copied definition with incompatible use.
One rehearsed sentence credited as functional classroom vocabulary across situations.
protocols.transfer: Use another classroom concept and a different practical exchange.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete vocabulary claim includes acquisition from talk/text, oral use and written application. Source early oral contribution is not a certificate of every broader whole-topic demand.

protocols.task: Provide familiar-meaning English words of two or more syllables in new printed order. Ask the child to decode chunks, identify their vowel sounds and blend the whole word.
evidenceDesign: Distinguish actual printed-word decoding from oral syllable joining supplied by an adult.
Vary syllable patterns and test a fresh word within taught correspondences.
Retain both the vowel-sound and chunk/blend requirements of the whole existing claim.
nearMisses: Recognising only a memorised word picture.
Clapping a long spoken word while never reading it.
protocols.transfer: Read a new multisyllabic word and a short containing sentence.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The existing decoding claim is distinct from the oral Syllables operation. Its title’s age label does not justify another number/grade clone; actual claim meaning drives this mapping.

protocols.task: Declare a familiar taught English word set including regular patterns, common clusters and known frequent exceptions. Say selected words without showing them. The child analyses sounds where useful, retrieves known spellings where necessary and writes the words; distinguish these strategies rather than assume one sound-by-sound route spells every word.
evidenceDesign: Retain actual listening, sound analysis and written production.
Change the item so copying a displayed spelling cannot pass.
A broader dictated-sentence claim is not required for this word-level source operation.
Include an unfamiliar-to-task regular item, a taught cluster item and a known exception item; record the actual taught set so the task does not imply arbitrary-dictionary spelling.
nearMisses: Copying a visible word or reciting letter names without writing its sound sequence.
protocols.transfer: Write a new regular word with a different sound sequence.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: BhY retains CVC/simple regular encoding; the cluster claim retains initial/final clusters and two-syllable reading/writing; the exception claim retains known high-frequency spellings, all seven weekday spellings and a short dictated-sentence case when assessing that complete existing claim. Those broader canonical checks are not invented NCERT word-list mandates. Source evidence alone does not certify all phonics terminology prerequisites, and no additional dependency change is made.

protocols.task: Say a familiar English target word. The child chooses a genuine rhyme and writes it without copying an adult model, then explains the shared sound ending.
evidenceDesign: Check both audible rhyme and actual written encoding.
Include a visually similar non-rhyme and a changed target.
Use appropriate taught regular words for the full spelling-by-sound evidence; no claim to spell every possible English rhyme is made.
nearMisses: Writing a copied answer or selecting matching final letters with different sound.
protocols.transfer: Write a rhyme for a new target from a different word family.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The two existing rhyme and phonemic-encoding claims remain distinct; neither is replaced by the other and no new rhyme-writing clone is created.

protocols.task: Read and write English words with familiar initial and final consonant clusters, including one- and two-syllable cases within taught vowel/digraph patterns.
evidenceDesign: Retain every consonant sound in a cluster instead of dropping or inserting one.
Include reading and spelling, not only pronounce a supplied word.
Use a fresh familiar-meaning example so the source’s illustrative words do not become an exhaustive list.
nearMisses: Reading only the first consonant or writing a memorised word while dropping a sound on transfer.
protocols.transfer: Read/write a new word with another initial/final cluster combination.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The complete existing consonant-cluster reading/spelling claim is retained, including short/common long vowels, digraphs and two-syllable cases. No special Grade 2/India blend topic is created.

protocols.task: Let the child choose a suitable short English poem, learn it and recite it with intelligible expression. Offer a different choice or support where needed and keep the contextual response separate.
evidenceDesign: Retain actual performance, not only a statement about liking recitation.
For the complete recitation claim, include a useful visual support for an oral description and complete sentences in a short presentation.
Do not equate fluency, loudness or willingness to perform publicly with enjoyment.
nearMisses: Adult says every line first while the result is labelled memorised independent recitation.
Correct recital automatically credited as positive feelings.
protocols.transfer: Choose another short poem or perform for a different low-stakes listener.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: ZB contributes actual performance; its complete presentation/visual-support operation is not inferred from one recital. The mixed source requirement keeps a contextual channel without a forced enthusiasm score.

protocols.task: Use a shared meaningful picture to support an English description and a short exchange; change a detail or ask the child to respond to another view.
evidenceDesign: The picture supplies content, not every spoken response.
Retain intelligible detail, relevant multi-turn response and turn-giving.
Ask what the partner actually said rather than only name isolated objects.
nearMisses: Adult scripts the entire dialogue or accepts one label as a conversation.
protocols.transfer: Use another picture with a different situation and new partner.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The whole discussion/description claims are retained; visual support does not establish reading a written text or transfer another language’s vocabulary.

protocols.task: Use a suitable local/folk tale heard from a parent, elder or authorised elder telling/recording. Record that material context, then invite an English class retelling with identifiable people and an ordered event line.
evidenceDesign: Preserve the actual local/heard-telling context rather than relabel an unrelated commercial story.
Use appropriate authorised material and a child-safe alternative; do not fabricate a family observation or require personal disclosure.
Judge meaningful English retelling, not word-for-word translation or a new local-facts inventory.
nearMisses: Only naming a tale or copying an adult-completed English script.
protocols.transfer: Retell another suitably sourced tale or explain a changed event relation to a new listener.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The same story-element/description operation is reused. Local source material is a retained input condition, not a new country/folktale mastery claim.

protocols.task: In a small group with a familiar classroom topic, invite the child to start an exchange without supplying the first sentence, then respond to a peer and keep the topic meaningful.
evidenceDesign: Retain initiation as well as ongoing contribution.
Use appropriate known/acquired English words for the classroom concept.
Separate a fully prompted opening from an independently chosen start.
nearMisses: Only answering the adult’s supplied question while it is credited as initiating a group conversation.
protocols.transfer: Start another topic exchange with different peers.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The existing vocabulary-use and discussion operations cover the actual action; first-speaker status does not justify a duplicate conversation topic.
